name: Smith Brothers of Berne Inc
old_description: Today’s Smith Brothers of Berne owes its humble 1926 beginnings to Homer Neiderhauser and the Dunbar Furniture company. It began as a manufacturer of lower-price point chairs to supplement the high-end furniture being produced by Dunbar in Berne. Although it started as the Homer Manufacturing Company, its first manager, Orv Smith, and his brother Les Smith, soon bought a majority share in the company. From 1936 to 1960, the Smith brothers successfully grew their company in the shadow of the likes of Dunbar and Berne Furniture. They changed the name to the Smith Brothers Furniture Manufacturing Company.
about:
Smith Brothers of Berne traces its roots to 1926 in Berne, Indiana, where Homer Neiderhauser and the Dunbar Furniture Company established the Homer Manufacturing Company to produce lower-price point chairs that would supplement Dunbar’s high-end furniture lines. In 1936, Orv Smith and his brother Les Smith acquired a majority stake, renaming the business Smith Brothers Furniture Manufacturing Company and beginning a period of family-led growth that continued through 1960.

Today the company operates as a furniture manufacturer with a workforce of approximately 30 employees in Berne. Its production focuses on chairs and other wood furniture pieces, though specific processes, facility size, and annual volumes are not publicly disclosed. The company continues to operate under the Smith Brothers name, maintaining a legacy of mid-market furniture production.

The firm serves the residential and commercial furniture markets, but the input does not name specific industries or customer accounts beyond its original relationship with Dunbar Furniture. No further details on target sectors or client types are provided.

The business was founded to fill a gap in the market by offering affordable seating options alongside premium offerings, a positioning that the company cites as its founding purpose. The Smith brothers’ acquisition in 1936 set the stage for decades of independent operation in a region dominated by larger furniture makers.
